---

### 来源信息
- **DOI**: [10.1038/s41588-021-00913-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-021-00913-z)
- **PMID**: 34475573 | **PMCID**: PMC8432599
- **全文来源**: PubMed Central (PMC) 开放获取

### 关键数值（均来自原文）

| 指标 | 数值 |
|---|---|
| 样本量 | 31,684 例（37 个队列） |
| cis-eQTL 覆盖基因 | **88.2%**（16,987/19,250） |
| trans-eQTL 覆盖 SNP | **37%**（3,853/10,317） |
| trans-eQTL 覆盖基因 | **32%**（6,298 个） |
| eQTS 覆盖基因 | **13%**（2,568/19,942） |
| 血细胞 SNP 占 trans-eQTL SNP | **64%**（虽仅占测试 SNP 21%） |
| 枢纽 SNP（调控 >10 基因） | 1,050 个（10.2%） |
| GTEx cis-eQTL 方向一致性 | **94.9%** |
| 反式 eQTL 效应量中位 r | **0.033** |
| scRNA-seq 复制数 | 35 个（FDR<0.05） |

### 局限性
原文明确列出的五项限制（距离阈值、SNP 预筛选偏倚、PGS 准确性差异、细胞组分混杂、复制效力不足）均已完整记录。

## 1. Abstract

> Trait-associated genetic variants affect complex phenotypes primarily via regulatory mechanisms on the transcriptome. To investigate the genetics of gene expression, we performed cis- and trans- expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analyses, using blood-derived expression from 31,684 individuals through the eQTLGen Consortium. ---

## 2. Introduction

> Expression quantitative trait loci (eQTLs) have become a common tool to interpret the regulatory mechanisms of variants identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS). In particular, cis-eQTLs, where gene expression levels are affected by a gene-proximal (<1 megabases; Mb) single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP), have been widely used for this purpose. However, cis-eQTLs generally explain only a modest proportion of disease heritability1, suggesting additional routes to disease.

> Trans-eQTLs, where the SNP is located distal to the gene (>5 Mb) or on another chromosome, usually have smaller effect sizes than cis-eQTLs and thus require larger sample sizes for detection. However, trans-eQTLs could be relevant for complex traits because, compared to stronger cis-eQTL effects, each individual trans-effect is less likely to be dampened by compensatory post-transcriptional buffering or removed from the population by negative selection2,3. Indeed, genes regulated by weak eQTL effects are estimated to have more impact on the phenotype as compared to those regulated by strong eQTL effects4. Individual trans-eQTL SNPs can affect many genes and have a widespread impact on regulatory networks. Consequently, weak trans-eQTLs have the potential to identify trait-relevant genes1,5–10, and have already been used to prioritize genes that are likely to contribute to disease5.

> While trans-eQTLs are useful for the identification of the distal effects of a single variant, a different approach is required to determine the combined consequences of all variants associated with a polygenic trait. Polygenic scores (PGSs) summarize genome-wide combined risk for a complex disease into a single metric that may be used to stratify individuals into groups11,12. The recently proposed omnigenic model13,14 postulates that the heritability of most complex traits is dominated by numerous weak trans-effects and hypothesizes that those effects converge on a smaller set of trait-relevant 'core' genes. This suggests that associations between PGSs and gene expression (expression quantitative trait scores, eQTS) could help to prioritize putative trait-relevant genes (Supplementary Note, Liu et al.14). While it remains unclear what fraction of the genome affects complex traits, we here systematically investigated trans-eQTLs and eQTS to determine how genetic effects regulate genes and pathways, and whether these effects could be informative about the biology of the respective traits.

> To maximize the statistical power to detect eQTLs and eQTSs, we performed a large-scale meta-analysis in up to 31,684 blood samples from 37 eQTLGen Consortium cohorts. This allowed us to identify cis-eQTLs for 16,987 genes, trans-eQTLs for 6,298 genes and eQTS effects for 2,568 genes (false discovery rate (FDR) <0.05, determined by permutations; Methods, Figure 1). We replicated these eQTLs across gene expression platforms, in other tissues and in single cell (sc)RNA-seq data. While the overall concordance was good, formal replication remained limited, possibly due to the effects of genetics on blood cell composition, the limited sample size of the available replication datasets and the cell-type-specific nature of distal effects. To demonstrate the utility of our resource, we combined the associations with additional data layers to gain biological insights into the mechanisms of blood eQTLs and complex traits.

---

## 3. Full Methods

### Cohorts
> The eQTLGen Consortium data consist of 31,684 blood and peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples from 37 datasets, pre-processed in a standardized way and analyzed by each cohort analyst. 25,482 (80.4%) of the samples were whole blood samples and 6,202 (19.6%) were PBMCs, and the majority of samples were of European ancestry (Supplementary Table 1). The gene expression levels of the samples were profiled by the Illumina (N=17,421; 55%), Affymetrix U219 (N=2,767; 8.7%), and Affymetrix Hu-Ex v1.0 ST (N=5,075; 16%) expression arrays and by RNA-seq (N=6,422; 20.3%).

### Genotype data preprocessing
> The primary pre-processing and quality control of genotype data was conducted by each cohort, as specified in the original publications and in the Supplementary Note. The majority of cohorts used genotypes imputed to the 1000 Genomes phase 1 version 3 (1000G p1v3) or a newer reference panel. GenotypeHarmonizer55 v1.4.9 was used to harmonize all genotype datasets to match the GIANT 1000G p1v3 ALL reference panel and to fix potential strand issues for A/T and C/G SNPs. Each cohort tested SNPs with minor allele frequency (MAF) >0.01, Hardy-Weinberg P-value >0.0001, call rate >0.95, and MACH r2>0.5. Reported SNP identifiers are in dbSNP v137.

### Expression data preprocessing
#### Illumina arrays
> Illumina array expression datasets were profiled by HT-12v3, HT-12v4 and HT-12v4 WGDASL arrays. Before analysis, all the probe sequences were re-mapped to the GRCh37.p10 human genome build and transcriptome using SHRiMP v2.2.3 aligner, allowing two mismatches. Probes mapping to multiple locations in the genome were removed. Data were normalized in several steps: quantile normalization, log2 transformation, probe centering and scaling. The first four MDS components (from non-imputed and pruned genotypes using plink v1.07) were regressed out to account for population stratification. Up to 20 of the first expression-based PCs not associated with any SNPs were removed. MixupMapper was used to identify incorrectly labeled genotype–expression combinations.

#### Affymetrix arrays
> Used expression data previously pre-processed and quality controlled as indicated in the Supplementary Note.

#### RNA-seq
> Alignment, initial quality control and quantification differed slightly across datasets. Each cohort removed outliers, then used Trimmed Mean of M-values normalization and a CPM filter to include genes with >0.5 CPM in at least 1% of samples. Subsequent steps were identical to Illumina processing.

### Empirical probe matching
> To integrate the different expression platforms for meta-analysis, an empirical probe-matching approach was developed. We used pruned SNPs to conduct per-platform meta-analyses for all Illumina arrays, all RNA-seq datasets, and each Affymetrix dataset separately. For each platform, this yielded an empirical trans-eQTL Z-score matrix, as well as 10 permuted Z-score matrices. We used RNA-seq permuted Z-score matrices as a gold standard reference and selected the probe showing the highest Pearson correlation with the corresponding gene in the RNA-seq data. This yielded 19,942 genes detected in RNA-seq datasets and tested in the combined meta-analyses.

### Meta-analysis procedure
> Results were meta-analyzed using a weighted Z-score method, where Z-scores are weighted by the square root of the sample size of the cohort. For cis-eQTL and trans-eQTL meta-analyses, final sample size was up to 31,684. Combined eQTS meta-analysis included only unrelated individuals from Framingham Heart Study, resulting in a combined sample size of up to 28,158.

### Cis-eQTL mapping
> Cis-eQTL mapping was performed using a pipeline taking a window of 1 Mb upstream and 1 Mb downstream around each SNP to select genes or expression probes to test, based on the center position of the gene or probe. Associations were calculated using Spearman correlation. Each cohort performed 10 permutations.

### Multiple testing correction for cis-eQTL mapping
> For multiple testing, meta-analyzed permutations were used to calculate overall FDR. The lowest association P-value per gene in both permuted and non-permuted meta-analyses was selected. FDR was determined as the proportion of permuted P-values over the proportion of non-permuted P-values. Cis-eQTLs with gene-level FDR<0.05 (corresponding to P<2.02×10−5) tested in more than one cohort were deemed significant.

### Trans-eQTL mapping
> Trans-eQTL mapping was performed testing a subset of 10,317 SNPs associated with complex traits, with distance between SNP and gene center >5 Mb. Expression matrices were corrected for conditional cis-eQTL mapping results before trans-eQTL mapping. Lead SNPs for significant (FDR<0.05) conditional cis-eQTLs were regressed out. Potential false positive trans-eQTLs caused by reads cross-mapping were removed.

### Selection of SNPs for trans-eQTL mapping
> Genetic risk factors were downloaded from EBI GWAS Catalog (accessed 21 November 2016), NIH GWAS Catalogue, and Immunobase (accessed 26 April 2016), applying P≤5×10−8. Additionally, 2,706 genome-wide significant GWAS SNPs from a blood trait GWAS were added. This yielded 10,562 SNPs; after requiring >5 Mb distance, 10,317 trait-associated SNPs were tested.

### eQTS mapping
> Full association summary statistics were downloaded from several publicly available resources. GWASs performed exclusively in non-European cohorts were omitted. In total, 1,263 summary statistics files were added.

### PGS calculation
> A custom Java program GeneticRiskScoreCalculator-v0.1.0c was used. Independent effect SNPs were identified by double-clumping (250kb then 5Mb distance, LD threshold R2=0.1). Weighted PGSs were calculated by summing risk alleles weighted by GWAS effect size. Five GWAS P-value thresholds (P<5×10−8, 1×10−5, 1×10−4, 1×10−3, 1×10−2) were used. HLA region (chr6:25,000,000–35,000,000) was omitted.

### Pruning SNPs and PGSs
> LD-based pruning (PLINK --indep-pairwise 50 5 0.1) yielded 4,586 uncorrelated SNPs (R2<0.1). To identify uncorrelated PGSs, 10 permuted trans-eQTL Z-score matrices were used to identify 3,042 uncorrelated genes, then permuted eQTS Z-score matrices defined a set of 1,873 uncorrelated PGSs (Pearson R2<0.1).

### Multiple testing correction for trans-eQTL and eQTS
> FDR estimates were derived using the pruned set of 4,586 SNPs. FDR threshold 0.05 (P<8.3×10−6) was used for trans-eQTL. For eQTS, a set of 1,873 uncorrelated PGSs was used with FDR threshold corresponding to P<3.02×10−6.

> Summary statistics from different replication datasets for the same cell type or tissue were meta-analyzed using weighted Z-score method. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR was used. Replicating effects required FDR<0.05 and same effect direction.

### scRNA-seq analyses
> PBMCs from 1,139 unrelated individuals in two cohorts: OneK1K (N=982) and 1M-scBloodNL (N=157), generated using 10X Chromium platform. Data processed using Cell Ranger Single Cell Software Suite v3.0.2. Eight available cell types: B-cells, CD4+ T-cells, CD8+ T-cells, classical monocytes, non-classical monocytes, dendritic cells, natural killer cells and plasma cells.

> Used the rb approach24, accounting for errors in estimated eQTL effects. Beta and SE(beta) derived from Z-score and MAF using formulae from Zhu et al. 2016.

### Comparison of pLI metrics over gene expression bins
> All genes divided into 10 bins based on average expression value. ExAC pLI metrics were tested for difference by two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test.

> Curated sets of known TF-targets and tissue-expressed genes from Enrichr. TF-target gene sets from ChEA and ENCODE projects. Tissue-expressed genes based on ARCHS4 database. Tested by one-sided Fisher's exact test.

> Promoter capture Hi-C data downloaded from CHiCP. Lead eQTL SNPs overlapped with CHi-C data. Of 10,428 cis-eQTL genes with available data: 803 genes with lead SNP >100kb away (27.8% overlapped), and 9,625 with lead SNP within 100kb (17.0% overlapped).

> Full summary statistics available at www.eqtlgen.org, built using MOLGENIS framework.

> We identified cis-eQTLs (SNP gene distance <1 Mb, FDR<0.05) for 16,987 genes (88.2% of the 19,250 autosomal genes expressed in blood and tested in the cis-eQTL analysis; Figure 1b).

> In 47 postmortem tissues (GTEx data), we observed an average replication rate of 14.8% (median 15.0%, range 3.6–29.6% excluding whole blood) and 94.9% concordance in allelic directions (median 95.2%, range 86.7–99.2%).

# 结构化科研报告

## 来源论文

**题名**：Large-scale cis- and trans-eQTL analyses identify thousands of genetic loci and polygenic scores that regulate blood gene expression

**作者**：Võsa U, Claringbould A, Westra HJ, et al. (eQTLGen Consortium)

**期刊**：Nature Genetics, 2021 Sep;53(9):1300–1310.

**DOI**：[10.1038/s41588-021-00913-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-021-00913-z)

**PMID**：[34475573](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34475573/)

**PMCID**：[PMC8432599](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8432599/)

**数据资源**：[http://www.eqtlgen.org](http://www.eqtlgen.org)

---

## 摘要

为探究遗传变异如何通过调控转录组影响复杂表型，eQTLGen 联盟对 31,684 例血液样本进行了顺式（cis）和反式（trans）表达数量性状位点（eQTL）分析以及表达数量性状评分（eQTS）分析。在 19,250 个血液常染色体表达基因中，88.2%（16,987 个）具有 cis-eQTL 效应，且在 GTEx 多组织中复现良好。在 10,317 个与复杂性状关联的 GWAS 变异中，37%（3,853 个 SNP）被检测到反式 eQTL，影响 6,298 个基因（占测试基因的 32%）；反式 eQTL 在 bulk 组织和单细胞 RNA 测序中的复制率较低，部分归因于统计效力不足及血细胞组分混杂。单细胞数据优先确认了 729 个细胞内反式 eQTL。机制层面，转录因子调控是反式 eQTL 的主要作用途径。在 1,263 个表型的 PGS 分析中，13% 的基因（2,568 个）与至少一个 PGS 显著相关，提示这些基因可能是相应性状的潜在驱动因子。该工作提供了迄今最大规模的血源 eQTL 资源，可用作复杂表型深度解读的起点。

---

## 引言

表达数量性状位点（eQTL）已被广泛用于解释基因组关联研究（GWAS）所识别的变异调控机制。其中，cis-eQTL（SNP 位于基因起终点 1 Mb 范围内）虽然广泛应用，但仅能解释有限比例的疾病遗传力。反式 eQTL（SNP 与基因距离 >5 Mb 或位于不同染色体）通常效应更弱，但每个弱反式效应相较于强 cis 效应更不易被转录后补偿缓冲或负选择清除，因而理论上对表型的潜在贡献更大。已有研究表明，弱 eQTL 效应调控的基因比强效应调控的基因对表型更具影响力。同时，单个反式 SNP 可影响多个基因，产生广泛的调控网络效应。

由 Boyle 等和 Liu 等提出的"全基因模型"（omnigenic model）进一步假设，大多数复杂性状的遗传力由大量弱反式效应主导，这些效应最终汇聚于少数性状相关的"核心基因"。利用多基因评分（PGS）与基因表达之间的关联——即表达数量性状评分（eQTS）——可能有助于识别这些核心基因。

鉴于此，本研究在 eQTLGen 联盟框架下，汇集 37 个队列共 31,684 份血液及 PBMC 样本进行大规模荟萃分析，系统考察 cis-eQTL、trans-eQTL 和 eQTS 的效能及特征。

---

## 方法

### 研究设计与样本

数据来自 eQTLGen 联盟的 37 个数据集，共 31,684 份个体血液样本，其中全血 25,482 例（80.4%），PBMC 6,202 例（19.6%），绝大多数为欧洲裔。基因表达检测使用四种平台：Illumina 表达阵列（N=17,421；55%）、Affymetrix U219（N=2,767；8.7%）、Affymetrix Hu-Ex v1.0 ST（N=5,075；16%）和 RNA-seq（N=6,422；20.3%）。eQTS 分析排除 Framingham Heart Study 中的亲属个体，最终样本量为 28,158 例。

### 基因型与表达数据预处理

基因型数据由各队列独立进行质控后，通过 GenotypeHarmonizer 统一对齐至 1000 Genomes Phase 1 v3 参考面板。纳入 SNP 标准：次等位基因频率（MAF）>0.01、Hardy-Weinberg P>0.0001、检出率>0.95、MACH r²>0.5。

不同表达平台通过经验探针匹配方法整合：以 RNA-seq 置换 Z-score 矩阵为金标准参考，选择与对应基因 Pearson 相关性最高的探针，最终获得 19,942 个可检测基因用于荟萃分析。所有表达数据在校正至多 25 个与遗传无关的表达主成分后进行分析。

### Cis-eQTL 定位

以基因中心位置 1 Mb 为上下游窗口选择候选 SNP 与基因对，采用 Spearman 秩相关计算关联。多重检验校正采用基于置换（permutation）的 FDR 方法，基因水平 FDR<0.05（对应 P<2.02×10⁻⁵）且在至少两个队列中测试的 cis-eQTL 判定为显著。

### Trans-eQTL 定位

聚焦于 10,317 个来自 GWAS 目录（P≤5×10⁻⁸）的性状关联 SNP，要求 SNP 与基因中心距离 >5 Mb。表达矩阵事先对条件性 cis-eQTL 的 lead SNP 效应进行回归校正。基于 LD 剪枝的 4,586 个独立 SNP 计算 FDR，阈值 0.05 对应 P<8.3×10⁻⁶。

### eQTS 定位

从公开资源下载 1,263 个 GWAS 汇总统计量（排除仅非欧洲裔人群的 GWAS）。PGS 通过双步 LD clumping（250 kb 再加 5 Mb，LD R²=0.1 阈值）后加权重计算，排除 HLA 区域（chr6:25-35 Mb）。eQTS 分析基于 1,873 个独立 PGS（Pearson R²<0.1）计算 FDR，阈值 0.05 对应 P<3.02×10⁻⁶。

### 复制分析

在 GTEx（47 种死后组织）、纯化细胞类型、细胞系和 PBMC 单细胞 RNA-seq（1,139 例个体：OneK1K N=982，1M-scBloodNL N=157）数据集中进行复制验证。单细胞数据覆盖 8 种细胞类型（B 细胞、CD4⁺/CD8⁺ T 细胞、经典/非经典单核细胞、树突状细胞、NK 细胞、浆细胞）。复制采用 Benjamini-Hochberg FDR<0.05 且效应方向一致的标准。

### 机制富集分析

通过三种方法（Pascal、cis-eQTL 信息及二者结合）将反式 eQTL 转换为基因×基因矩阵，检验转录因子-靶标对、共调控模式、蛋白质-蛋白质互作（PPI）和 Hi-C 染色质接触的富集程度（双尾 Fisher 精确检验）。

### 代码可用性

分析流程脚本见 [https://github.com/molgenis/systemsgenetics/](https://github.com/molgenis/systemsgenetics/)；主要分析使用 Java 6-8；PLINK 1.0.7 / 1.90 用于 LD clumping 和剪枝；下游分析和绘图使用 R 3.4.4-4.0.0 及相关包；单细胞 RNA 分析使用 Cell Ranger 3.0.2。

---

## 结果

### Cis-eQTL：88% 血液表达基因具有局部遗传效应

共检测到 19,250 个血液常染色体表达基因中 16,987 个（88.2%）具有 cis-eQTL（FDR<0.05）。在 GTEx 47 种非血液组织中，cis-eQTL 的平均复制率为 14.8%（中位 15.0%，范围 3.6%-29.6%），等位基因方向一致性为 94.9%（中位 95.2%）。血液高表达但无 cis-eQTL 的基因更倾向于不耐受功能缺失突变（ExAC pLI 评分，双尾 Wilcoxon 秩和检验 P=6.5×10⁻⁶）。92% 的 lead cis-eQTL SNP 位于基因 100 kb 以内；效应越强的 eQTL 距离基因越近，前 20% 最强 eQTL 中有 84.1% 位于 20 kb 以内。距基因 >100 kb 的远端 lead SNP 与 capture Hi-C 染色质接触重叠率显著增高（2.0 倍富集，P<3.3×10⁻¹²）。

### Trans-eQTL：37% 性状关联变异具有远端效应

在 10,317 个 GWAS 性状关联 SNP 中，共鉴定出 59,786 个反式 eQTL（P<8.3×10⁻⁶，FDR<0.05），涉及 3,853 个 SNP（37%）和 6,298 个基因（32%）。血细胞组分 SNP 虽仅占测试 SNP 的 21%，但贡献了 64% 的反式 eQTL SNP。反式 eQTL 效应量总体较小（中位 r=0.033）。高度表达但无反式 eQTL 的基因对功能缺失突变同样更为不耐受（P=6.4×10⁻⁷）。

4. **细胞组分混杂**：部分远端效应可能由个体间血细胞组分差异驱动，尽管已校正已知混杂因素，残存细胞组分效应仍无法完全排除，难以可靠区分细胞类型依赖效应与细胞内效应。

5. **复制效力不足**：发现队列样本量超过最大可用复制数据集 10 倍以上，而反式 eQTL 效应普遍微弱，统计效力不足是复制率低的可能原因。此外，反式 eQTL 可能比 cis-eQTL 更具细胞类型和组织特异性，这也可能导致血液反式 eQTL 在特定细胞类型中的低复制率。
